THE RECIPE SHELF / 01
Focaccia
2 h 25 min + prep
DOUGH
320 ml water
3 g yeast
5 g honey
10 g salt
400 g flour
TO FINISH
Rosemary, oregano, salt, garlic, and olive oil (amounts not specified)
INSTRUCTIONS
1. Mix half the water with the yeast and honey. Add the flour and mix briefly.
2. Add the salt and remaining water. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
3. Fold the edges into the centre all the way around. Cover and rest for 60 minutes.
4. Oil your hands and transfer the dough to an oiled baking pan. Cover and rest for 40 minutes.
5. Add rosemary, oregano, salt, garlic, and olive oil. Bake at 230°C for 15–20 minutes.

THE RECIPE SHELF / 02
Chocolate crinkles
20 min bake + chilling
INGREDIENTS
225 g dark chocolate
60 g butter
50 g brown sugar
2 eggs
225 g flour
Baking powder (amount not specified)
Vanilla extract (amount not specified)
Granulated and icing sugar, for coating (amounts not specified)
INSTRUCTIONS
1. Melt the chocolate and butter together over a water bath.

6. Bake at 170°C for 20 minutes.

THE RECIPE SHELF / 06
Doctor’s protein bars
30 min chill + prep & set
INGREDIENTS · MAKES 12
100 g Medjool dates, roughly chopped
250 g crunchy peanut butter
125 g unflavoured plant-based protein powder
100 g ground almonds
75 g milled chia seeds
2 tbsp maple syrup
175 ml water, plus extra boiling water to soak dates
150 g dark chocolate (80%), roughly chopped
Optional toppings of your choice
INSTRUCTIONS
1. Line a 20 × 20 cm baking tin with parchment paper.
2. Cover the dates with just enough boiling water. Soak for 10 minutes, then mash into a spreadable paste.
3. Blend the peanut butter, protein powder, ground almonds, chia, maple syrup, and 175 ml water in a food processor until smooth. Press into the tin, then spread the dates evenly on top.
4. Refrigerate for 30 minutes until firm. Cut into 12 bars.
5. Melt the chocolate in a bowl over a pan of simmering water, keeping the bowl clear of the pan base.
6. Set a wire rack over a tray. Dip the bars in chocolate, then leave on the rack so excess drips off. Add optional toppings while wet. Set for 5–10 minutes and store in the fridge.

Yield of 12 bars is from the original recipe. All 150 g coating chocolate is counted; drips and optional toppings are not adjusted.

White chocolate ice cream
Chill & churn
INGREDIENTS
100 ml milk
100 ml + 200 ml heavy cream
3 egg yolks
100 g white chocolate
50 g sugar
½ vanilla pod
INSTRUCTIONS

4. Pour over the chocolate and let it melt. Refrigerate the mixture.
5. Whisk the remaining 200 ml cream, then fold it into the chilled mixture.
6. Churn in an ice cream machine.

THE RECIPE SHELF / 12
Coffee ice cream
45 min steep + chill & churn
INGREDIENTS
235 ml milk
235 ml heavy cream, divided into two 117.5 ml portions
75 g coffee beans
50 g sugar
3 egg yolks
2 g salt
INSTRUCTIONS
1. Combine the milk, 117.5 ml cream, sugar, salt, and coffee beans. Heat almost to boiling, cover, and steep for 45 minutes.
2. Put the remaining 117.5 ml cream in a bowl set over an ice bath.
3. Reheat the coffee mixture to almost boiling. Slowly whisk a little into the egg yolks, then return everything to the pot.
4. Stir until slightly thickened.
5. Strain out the coffee beans, pouring the custard into the cream over the ice bath.
6. Churn in an ice cream machine.
RECIPE NOTE: Chilling and churning times are not specified in the original notes; follow your machine’s instructions.
